name: inprocess-wb-apb-pulp-i2c-fuzz
notes: the same PULP apb_i2c APB3 target and the same fixed pad inputs as inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-i2c-fuzz.json, now driven by one PicoRV32 Wishbone CPU; no CPU x IP code is added, only the CPU profile and the RAM image change
the RAM image starts at 0 because this CPU's own boot contract declares reset_vector 0; the entry takes the boot address from that contract and refuses an image that does not contain it
the target window is the I2C profile's 4 KiB APB window at 0x40000000

this CPU declares a 32-bit irq vector and no per-bit wiring is declared for it, so the host holds it at zero and F5 is refused by name; the I2C profile also declares no interrupt source, so F5 would be unavailable either way
no DMA model is declared, so F6 is refused by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB)
the cpu and target declare 50 MHz, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives both models
